title: Temperature-Controlled Assembly and Characterization of a Droplet Interface Bilayer
protocol: Gather 2 pieces of 1 mm thick insulative rubber trimmed to 25 mm x 40 mm.
Gather 2 pieces of a 6 mm-thick rubber also trimmed to 25 mm x 40 mm.
Prepare an aluminum base fixture assembly.
Prepare an acrylic oil reservoir that fits in the viewing window of the aluminum base fixture.
Attach a glass coverslip viewing window with UV curable adhesive to the bottom of the aluminum fixture.
Adhere one resistive heating element to the top of each 25 mm x 25 mm side flange of the fixture.
Place thinner rubber pieces onto the stage of the microscope tangential to the stage opening.
Position the aluminum-base fixture on top of the insulative pads with the viewing window centered above the objective lens.
Place a thicker piece of rubber on top of each resistive heating element.
Use a microscope stage clip to hold the thick rubber pieces in place.
Carefully bend the measurement-end of a thermocouple to achieve a 90° angle at ~4 mm from the end.
Insert the bent tip of the thermocouple into the lower left corner of the aluminum fixture.
Secure the thermocouple with the locking screw.
Place the acrylic reservoir into the well of the aluminum fixture.
Dispense approximately 1,000 µL of hexadecane oil into the well of the aluminum fixture.
Ensure the oil level in the well does not overfill and spill over the edges.
Dispense approximately 1,000 µL of hexadecane oil into the acrylic reservoir.
Avoid overfilling the acrylic reservoir.
Thoroughly clean the acrylic reservoir between experiments.
Rinse the acrylic reservoir successively with ethyl-alcohol and deionized water.
Dry the acrylic reservoir in a desiccator bowl for over 12 hours.
Establish output and input connections to the DAQ-2 modules.
Select two pairs of screw terminals on the voltage output module for differential voltage connections.
Attach wire leads to these locations.
Connect each pair of lead wires to separate screw-terminal-BNC adapters.
Connect each adapter to a separate BNC cable used to route voltage signals to other instruments.
Assign differential connections at terminals 0 and 1 for the temperature control output to the power amplifier.
Designate another pair of connections at terminals 6 and 7 for voltage output to be sent to the droplets via the patch clamp amplifier.
Select one set of thermocouple terminals (e.g., terminals 2 and 3 are designated as the TC1 pair) on the thermocouple input module.
Connect the thermocouple wires to the selected terminal pair.
Connect the DAQ-2 chassis to a PC via a USB connection.
Connect the DAQ-2 chassis to an electrical power source.
Confirm successful driver and software installation prior to use with commercial software.
Configure and connect a power amplifier between DAQ-2 and resistive heating elements.
Configure the amplifier to operate in fixed-gain amplification mode with a gain of 10X.
Using a banana jack-BNC adapter, connect the BNC cable originating from terminals 0 and 1 on the voltage output module to the input connections on the power amplifier.
Connect the output terminals of the power amplifier to both sets of heating elements using BNC adapters and cabling.
Establish necessary connections for the electrophysiology equipment.
Connect a BNC cable from terminals 6 and 7 on the voltage output module to the Rear Switched External Command BNC connectors on the patch clamp amplifier.
Connect a second BNC cable between the output of waveform generator and the Front Switch External Command connection on the rear of the patch clamp amplifier.
Connect the output of the measured current located on the front panel of the patch clamp amplifier to an available analog input BNC connector on DAQ-1.
Connect the output of measured membrane voltage from the rear of the patch clamp amplifier to a separate analog input connector on DAQ-1.
Connect the electrode leads to the patch clamp headstage.
Attach the patch clamp headstage via cable to the patch clamp amplifier.
Connect DAQ-1 to a PC via USB connection.
Connect power supply cables to both the patch clamp amplifier and DAQ-1.
Power on all measurement equipment.
Ensure the power amplifier output connections are electrically isolated from the headstage unit.
Start the DAQ-2 software on the PC.
Open the temperature control program file.
Once the GUI opens, open the program again by clicking on the folder icon in the bottom left corner of the GUI.
Select the temperature control program.
Enter appropriate numerical values for the proportional control gain (KP).
Enter appropriate numerical values for the integral control gain (KI).
Lower the tips of the silver/silver chloride electrodes into the oil until they nearly touch the bottom of the acrylic reservoir.
Pipette a 250 nL droplet of aqueous lipid solution containing 2 mg/mL of BTLE, 100 mM potassium chloride (KCl), and 10 mM MOPS onto each electrode tip.
Let the droplets incubate in the heated oil for a minimum of 10 minutes to promote monolayer formation.
Cover the headstage and heated stage fixture with a grounded Faraday cage.
Bring the droplets into gentle contact by slowly manipulating the horizontal positions of the electrodes until the user sees the droplets deform from contact or begin to displace one another.
Wait a few minutes until bilayer formation commences.
If after several minutes a bilayer has not formed, coerce the droplets together more to facilitate bilayer formation.
Confirm the formation of a thinned interfacial bilayer through visual inspection.
Measure the increase in the amplitude of a square-waveform capacitive current induced by a waveform generator outputting a 10 mV, 10 Hz triangular voltage.
Allow the bilayer to equilibrate for a minimum of 10 minutes to reach a steady interfacial area upon initial formation.

Measure the nominal capacitance of the membrane while lowering the temperature of the oil bath from a set point that permits bilayer formation to identify thermotropic phase transitions of the lipids in the membrane.
Right click the temperature graph on the GUI and clear the displayed data.
Apply a triangular voltage waveform across the DIB electrodes using the waveform generator connected to the patch clamp amplifier.
Record the induced current response through the bilayer.
Reduce the set point temperature in 5 °C increments and wait at least 5 min between each increment until reaching the desired minimum temperature.
Cool the bilayer by turning off the feedback control system if passively cooling.
Right click the temperature graph in the GUI again and export the temperature data versus time to a spreadsheet software.
Stop the current recording.
Calculate the nominal capacitance of the square wave-current response versus time during the cooling period from the measured current.
Plot nominal capacitance (C) versus temperature (T).
Locate nonmonotonic changes in C versus T to identify TM.
Change the set point temperature in 10 °C increments using the GUI and allow the system to equilibrate to the new temperature.
Initiate the measurement of capacitive current and recording.
Adjust the positions of the electrodes using micro-manipulators to change the bilayer area.
Allow for the square-wave current to reach a steady state amplitude.
Collect images of the DIB to enable calculation of membrane area versus time.
Add a digital tag in the current recording software to mark the corresponding timepoint for image collection.
Repeat Step 4.2.1.2 a minimum of 4 times to obtain a total of 5 DIB images and steady-state regions of bilayer current.
Repeat Step 4.2.1 at each desired temperature.
At the tagged timepoints corresponding to steady-state bilayer areas for acquired images, analyze the current recordings and DIB images to extract C and A data for each temperature.
Plot C versus A data for each temperature and compute the slope of a first-order regression, which represents the Cm of the bilayer at each temperature.
Plot values of Cm obtained from Step 4.2.4 versus T.
Examine the Cm versus T data for non-monotonic variations to identify melting temperatures, TM.
Assess the dynamics of voltage-dependent ion channel formation by generating a dc voltage step input across the bilayer.
Set Initial Voltage to the desired step value in mV (e.g., 100 mV).
Set Final Voltage and Step Size to a value higher than the desired step (e.g., 110 mV final voltage and 110 mV step size).
Set a desired duration time for the step input in seconds (e.g., 90 s).
Choose the desired polarity for the step input (e.g., positive).
Switch the patch clamp amplifier to send to the headstage the command voltage originating from the GUI/voltage output module.
Initiate current recordings.
Turn on the voltage and record the induced current response.
Switch the patch clamp amplifier to send to the headstage the command voltage originating from the waveform generator.
Initiate current recordings.
On the waveform generator, output a continuous sinusoidal waveform with a desired amplitude, offset, and frequency.
Record the induced current response across one or multiple cycles.
